Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and
Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v.
Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
— Dispute over Technology Transfer Contract

【Ruling Summary】

In determining the validity of a contract, the criterion should be whether the contract violates the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, rather than determining the contract invalid on the ground that it violates the provisions of administrative rules. In a technology contract dispute, if the products or services involved in the technology contract are subject to administrative approval or license according to law but have not obtained such approval or license, this does not affect the validity of the relevant technology contract concluded between the parties.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 307

Reapplying Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit 1B, Building 2, Olympic Garden, No. 96 Haixiu Middle Road, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Tang Xiaodong, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Yu Yi, lawyer of Shandong Defu Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Ji Hongwei, lawyer of Shandong Defu Law Firm.

Reapplying Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 269 Nanhai Avenue, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Gao Yuwen, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yu Yi, lawyer of Shandong Defu Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Ji Hongwei, lawyer of Shandong Defu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: A11, Haikou Free Trade Zone, No. 168 Nanhai Avenue, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Han Yudong, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Lu Taishan, lawyer of Hainan New Concept Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Ji Jingwu, lawyer of Beijing Dacheng Law Firm.

The reapplying petitioners, Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangliyuan Company) and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangli Pharmaceutical Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2009) Qiong Min Er Zhong Zi No. 16 of the Hainan High People's Court regarding their dispute with the respondent, Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qili Pharmaceutical Company), over a technology transfer contract. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 713 on August 24, 2011, deciding to retry this case. This Court formed a collegiate panel according to law and held a public hearing of this case on October 26, 2011. The agents ad litem of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, Yu Yi, and the agents ad litem of Qili Pharmaceutical Company, Lu Taishan and Ji Jingwu, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) found the following facts upon trial: Kangliyuan Company was established on September 16, 1998, has the status of a legal person, and has obtained the *Drug Trading License* and the *Certificate of Compliance with Good Supply Practice for Pharmaceutical Products*. The original corporate name of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company was Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., which was established on May 16, 2000, has the status of a legal person, and has obtained the *Drug Manufacturing License* and the *Certificate of Compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products* (hereinafter referred to as Drug GMP Certificate) (Certificate Nos.: Qiong F0011, F0057, D1303, D1819, H3894-1, H3894-2). On December 31, 2006, the said Drug GMP Certificates were withdrawn by the Hainan Food and Drug Administration (hereinafter referred to as Hainan FDA). On February 20, 2008, upon approval of the change of registration by the Hainan Administration for Industry and Commerce, Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. changed its name to the current corporate name. Kangliyuan Company is a shareholder of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, originally holding 73% of the shares of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. After the change of registration of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, Kangliyuan Company held 22% of the shares of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and the remaining 51% of the shares were held by General Technology Group Medical Holdings Co., Ltd. Qili Pharmaceutical Company was established on August 28, 1997, has the status of a legal person, and has obtained the *Drug Manufacturing License* and Drug GMP Certificates (Certificate Nos.: Qiong G0055, Qiong G0063, G0062, G3601-1, G3601-2, Qiong H0097, F3035, J4636).

On April 26, 2000, Kangliyuan Company and Qili Pharmaceutical Company entered into the *Agreement on Cooperative Development, Production, and Operation of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection* (hereinafter referred to as the *April 26 Agreement*). In this agreement, Kangliyuan Company was Party A and Qili Pharmaceutical Company was Party B, stipulating the following: Party A contributed RMB 1,000,000 and Party B contributed RMB 500,000, and the two parties jointly developed Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (powder for injection, specification 1g/vial) and applied for the New Drug Certificate in the names of both parties, with the specific work to be implemented by Party B, who should complete and obtain the New Drug Certificate and production approval number issued by the State Food and Drug Administration (hereinafter referred to as the SFDA) as soon as possible; the property rights of the product were jointly owned by both parties, with Party A keeping the New Drug Certificate or all materials of the product; after obtaining the approval number, Party A was responsible for the costs of raw and auxiliary materials required for the production of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection and had full authority over the sales of the product, and the words "General Distribution by Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd." should be printed on the entire packaging; Party B should not process or sell the above products with any unit or individual other than Party A; Party B should provide factory premises, equipment, and technical personnel to produce the product in quality and quantity according to the quality standard of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection and the requirements of the "Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products"; Party B should strictly control unit consumption of materials and production costs; if losses of raw and auxiliary materials or finished products occurred due to poor production management, Party B should bear full responsibility; when Party A sold Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection, Party A should extract RMB 1.5 per vial from the sales profit as production profit for Party B, and pay an additional production cost of RMB 0.2 per vial; the annual production profit returned by Party A to Party B should not be less than RMB 400,000. The parties also agreed in an appendix to the agreement: on the premise that Party B guaranteed to invest RMB 1,500,000 in the development of the product Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (4:0.5) 1.0g/vial, Party A should invest RMB 1,000,000 according to the investment ratio of 2:1, and the balance should be invested by Party B who should implement all work for product development; upon signing of the agreement, Party A should immediately invest RMB 100,000 as preliminary expenses; before June 2000, Party B should complete all preclinical trial data, and Party A should invest RMB 170,000; when the product was submitted to the provincial and national evaluation, Party A should invest another RMB 170,000; once the clinical study of the product was approved and accepted (subject to the public announcement), Party A should invest development costs of RMB 350,000; upon completion of the clinical study of the product and obtaining the New Drug Certificate and production approval, Party A should pay another RMB 50,000; when Party B handed over the New Drug Certificate or all materials of the product to Party A for safekeeping, Party A should invest another RMB 80,000; and from the time Party A obtained the product produced by Party B for sales activities, Party A should pay the remaining development funds of RMB 80,000. After the agreement was signed, Kangliyuan Company made payments of RMB 100,000 on April 28, 2000, RMB 100,000 on June 8 of the same year, RMB 200,000 on August 31 of the same year, and RMB 100,000 on November 27 of the same year.

On June 8, 2001, Qili Pharmaceutical Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company entered into the *Agreement on Cooperative Development of the New Drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (1.2 g/vial)* (hereinafter referred to as the *June 8 Agreement*). In this agreement, Qili Pharmaceutical Company was Party A and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company was Party B, stipulating that: the two parties cooperated in developing and researching the new drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection with a specification of 1.2g/vial; Party A was responsible for the technical work of development and research, and Party B was responsible for providing the funds for development and research; the total amount of funds invested by Party B was RMB 2,880,000, and if clinical trials were waived, the total amount of funds invested was RMB 1,980,000; starting from July 2001, a monthly payment of RMB 250,000 should be made until the total was paid; Party A should accelerate the progress of research and development, calculated from January 2001; at each stage of the new drug evaluation, if the evaluation exceeded the time limit stipulated by the national evaluation regulations, Party A should give a reasonable explanation to Party B; if due to Party A's reasons the time limit exceeded 120 days, Party B had the right to terminate this agreement and withdraw the invested funds; after Party B invested the funds, if Party A could not continue the research and development work due to technical reasons, Party A had the responsibility to promptly notify Party B and refund all funds; when Party A was responsible for obtaining the clinical trial approval document for the drug, Party B's payment should reach RMB 1,000,000; when Party A was responsible for completing the clinical trial of the drug and gradually transferring the existing data to Party B; when Party B's payment reached RMB 2,000,000, Party A should be responsible for obtaining the New Drug Certificate and production approval for the drug; when Party B's payment reached RMB 2,500,000, the New Drug Certificate, production approval, and other materials should be fully transferred to Party B, and thereafter the property rights of the product belonged to Party B; Party A should assist Party B in producing three batches of qualified products before Party B paid the remaining development funds of RMB 380,000; after this agreement took effect, when Party A submitted relevant materials of the drug to the drug evaluation and drug inspection departments, the new drug research units should be jointly named by both parties; when applying for the production approval, the production unit of the drug should be declared as Party B; Party B was responsible for the production and sales of the product on its own; Party A should transfer all technology unreservedly to Party B and send personnel to Party B's premises to guide production, ensuring that Party B could independently trial-produce three consecutive batches of products meeting quality standards; Party B had the exclusive right to receive and produce the new drug, and Party A should not transfer the new drug to other parties and should not provide any materials of the new drug to other parties; otherwise, Party A should pay Party B liquidated damages equal to twice the contract amount; after this agreement took effect, the *April 26 Agreement* remained valid until Party B obtained the New Drug Certificate and production approval for the drug. After the agreement was signed, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company made payments of RMB 250,000 on July 18 and September 21, 2001, and RMB 100,000 on October 15, 2002.

After the above two agreements were signed, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid a total of RMB 1,100,000.

On June 12, 2004, Qili Pharmaceutical Company, Kangliyuan Company, and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company entered into the *Contract on Transfer of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection* (hereinafter referred to as the *Transfer Contract*). In this contract, Qili Pharmaceutical Company was Party A, and Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were Party B. The preamble of the contract stated: "Due to changes in national policies and actual circumstances, the *Agreement on Cooperative Development of the New Drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (1.2 g/vial)* signed between Party A and Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. on June 8, 2001, shall no longer be performed. Through friendly negotiation between the parties, the following agreement is hereby entered into regarding the transfer of the new drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification 1.125 g/vial)." The main contents of the agreement were: 1. After Party A completes the ongoing Phase II clinical trial of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection, Party A shall immediately apply to the national drug regulatory authority for the New Drug Certificate and production approval, and after obtaining approval, transfer the product with a specification of 1.125g/vial to Party B, and Party B agrees to accept the transfer; 2. After the transfer is completed, the ownership of the product with this specification shall belong to Party B; Party A shall provide Party B with a complete set of copies of materials (including clinical materials) related to the product with this specification. Phase III clinical work shall be responsible by Party A, with costs borne by Party A; however, if Party B increases cases, the costs for the increased portion shall be borne by Party B; 3. Due to constraints of relevant drug regulatory regulations, the production unit stated on the production approval of the product with this specification shall still be Party A. However, Party A undertakes that, after obtaining the production approval, it will actively cooperate with Party B to handle the commissioned processing procedures, and immediately after approval, transfer the product to Party B for production; Party A shall send personnel to guide Party B in producing three consecutive batches of qualified products; 4. The transfer price is RMB 3,000,000; within 7 days from the date of obtaining the production approval, Party B shall pay 80%, i.e., RMB 2,400,000; within 7 days from the date of completing the commissioned processing procedures, Party B shall pay the remaining 20% balance of RMB 600,000. Party A shall issue an invoice for the development costs of the product with this specification to Party B. The date on which Party B pays off all transfer payments shall be deemed the date of completion of the transfer; 5. From the date of completion of the transfer, the costs for maintaining the drug approval number of this specification shall be borne by Party B. The three parties also agreed in the contract: from the effective date of this contract, Party A shall no longer discuss cooperation or transfer matters regarding this specification product with third parties; after Party B pays off 80% of the transfer payment, Party A undertakes not to produce or sell this specification product; after the transfer is completed, Party A shall no longer own this specification product; Party B shall exclusively own this specification product and be responsible for its production and sales; for problems arising during production and sales, if Party A is held jointly and severally liable due to the production approval being under Party A's name, all losses caused to Party A shall be borne by Party B; in the future, when Party B needs Party A to issue relevant procedures due to production or sales needs, Party A shall cooperate, but all costs shall be borne by Party B; both parties shall consciously abide by the contract provisions; any party that breaches the contract provisions shall fully compensate the non-breaching party for economic losses caused by the breach; from the effective date of this contract, the *April 26 Agreement* signed between the parties and the *June 8 Agreement* signed between Party A and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company shall automatically become invalid and shall no longer be binding on the parties.

On December 31, 2006, Hainan FDA issued a *Notice on Withdrawal of the Drug GMP Certificate of Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.* to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, stating that the company's drug production did not comply with the requirements of the *Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products*, and decided to withdraw its Drug GMP Certificates numbered Qiong F0011, Qiong G0057, D1303, D1819, H3894-1, and H3894-2, and required the company to carry out serious rectification in accordance with Drug GMP standards, and after completion of rectification, apply for re-inspection according to legal procedures. On May 21, 2007, the SFDA issued to Qili Pharmaceutical Company a *New Drug Certificate* with certificate number Guoyao Zheng Zi H20070099, which stated the drug name as "Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection". On the same day, Qili Pharmaceutical Company obtained two *Drug Registration Approval* issued by the SFDA, with approval numbers "2007S00839" and "2007S00840". Both approvals stated the drug name as "Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection", with a drug monitoring period of 4 years until May 20, 2011. Among them, approval number 2007S00839 stated the specification as "1.125g" and the drug approval number as "Guoyao Zhun Zi H20070233"; approval number 2007S00840 stated the specification as "2.25g" and the drug approval number as "Guoyao Zhun Zi H20070234".

On August 6, 2007, Qili Pharmaceutical Company sent a *Letter on Termination of the *Transfer Contract* between the Parties* to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, stating in the letter: "Due to major changes on your side, for a considerable period of time you do not meet the basic conditions stipulated by pharmaceutical regulations for accepting commissioned processing; the original contract cannot be performed. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, the original contract should be terminated. In order to reduce losses for both parties and ensure that the new drug can be promptly marketed and serve society, please send personnel to our side to negotiate refund and contract termination matters before August 20. If you do not send personnel for negotiation or reply after August 20, it shall be deemed that you agree to terminate the contract, the original contract shall be naturally terminated, and our side will refund you the amount according to the financial records." After receiving the letter, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company replied to Qili Pharmaceutical Company on August 16 of the same year, stating: "We are pleased to hear that the new drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (1.125g/vial) that we cooperatively developed and researched is about to obtain the production approval from the pharmaceutical regulatory authority, which is good news for both parties... At present, our contract party, Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., is operating normally, and Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is undergoing GMP hardware and software renovation. Regarding your proposal to terminate the contract on August 6, 2007, after careful consideration, our reply is as follows: ① We believe that the *Contract on Transfer of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection* signed by both parties on June 12, 2004, should continue to be performed in good faith; ② The reasons given by your side for terminating the contract are without factual and legal basis; therefore, neither party has the right to unilaterally terminate the contract; ③ After obtaining the product registration approval and before completing the transfer procedures, we are willing to negotiate with your side to cooperate on a mutually beneficial basis, striving for the early launch of the new drug." On August 23 of the same year, Qili Pharmaceutical Company replied to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company regarding the above reply, asserting that its termination of the original contract between the parties had sufficient factual and legal basis, and requested Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to send personnel before September 5 of the same year to discuss the specific matters of terminating the contract; if they did not send personnel for negotiation by that time, it would be deemed that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company agreed to terminate the contract, and the original contract would naturally lose effect and no longer be binding on them.

On January 14, 2008, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company applied to the court of first instance for pre-litigation preservation, requesting a ruling that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cease production and sales of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection with a specification of 1.125g/vial. Based on the above application of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, the court of first instance made the civil ruling (2008) Hai Zhong Fa Bao Zi No. 5 on January 21 of the same year, ordering Qili Pharmaceutical Company to cease production and sales of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection with a specification of 1.125g/vial from the date of receipt of the ruling. On February 4 of the same year, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company filed the present lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. A judgment ordering Qili Pharmaceutical Company to cease its breach of contract, cease production and sales of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification 1.125g/vial), and cease discussing cooperation or transfer matters regarding this specification product with third parties; 2. A judgment ordering Qili Pharmaceutical Company to continue performing the contract: (1) To issue relevant procedures in accordance with the contract to cooperate with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company (or an enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company) in production and sales, and immediately handle the transfer procedures to return the production right and sales right to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; (2) To provide Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company with a complete set of copies of materials (including clinical materials) of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification 1.125g/vial) in accordance with the contract; (3) To be responsible for sending personnel to guide Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company (or an enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company) in the continuous production of three batches of qualified products in accordance with the contract.

On February 22, 2008, Qili Pharmaceutical Company served on Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company a "Notice on Termination of the 'Contract for the Transfer of the New Drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection'." The notice stated that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had "seriously violated national laws and regulations, and the State Food and Drug Administration had revoked your company's GMP certification for drug production in January 2007," "your company has lost the statutory conditions for accepting the transfer of the new drug as agreed in the above contract," and "your company does not meet the statutory conditions for commissioned production of new drugs," and therefore decided to terminate the "Transfer Contract" signed between the parties. It further stated that if Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company believed they still met the conditions for accepting the new drug as agreed, they should submit the "Drug Manufacturing License" and the GMP certificate within five working days after receiving the notice; otherwise, it would be deemed that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company "cannot produce the new drug due to special reasons" and the contract would be automatically terminated. Thereafter, upon reviewing the objection to the pre-litigation preservation raised by Qili Pharmaceutical Company, the court of first instance rendered a civil ruling (2008) Hai Zhong Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 19-2 on May 26 of the same year, lifting the interim measure ordering Qili Pharmaceutical Company to cease production and sale of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification: 1.125g/bottle). During the first instance trial, the court of first instance investigated and collected evidence from the Hainan Drug Administration, which replied by letter confirming: 1. That administration had revoked, as required by the State Food and Drug Administration, GMP certificates numbered Qiong F0011, Qiong G0057, D1303, D1819, H3894-1, and H3894-2 issued to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; 2. Kangli Pharmaceutical Company held a Drug Manufacturing License; 3. Kangliyuan Company did not hold a Drug Manufacturing License or a GMP certificate.

The court of first instance further found: After obtaining the above "New Drug Certificate" and "Drug Registration Approval," Qili Pharmaceutical Company commenced production on its own and, starting in December 2007, engaged its wholly-owned subsidiary Haikou Qili Tongde Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to entrust companies including Guangzhou Xiuke Medical Technology Co., Ltd. and individuals including Luo Zhandou with agency sales.

The court of first instance held: The dispute between Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company arose from the performance of the "Transfer Contract" signed by the three parties. The dispute between the litigants involved the following issues: 1. Whether there was a connection between the "Transfer Contract" giving rise to the dispute and the agreements signed by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company with Qili Pharmaceutical Company on April 26, 2000, and June 8, 2001, respectively; 2. Whether the subject matter of the transfer under the "Transfer Contract" was a drug product or drug technology; 3. Whether Qili Pharmaceutical Company was entitled to terminate the "Transfer Contract"; 4. Whether the "Transfer Contract" could continue to be performed.

First, regarding the issue of contract connection. Prior to the execution of the "Transfer Contract" giving rise to the dispute, Kangliyuan Company and Qili Pharmaceutical Company entered into the "April 26 Agreement," in which they agreed to jointly develop, produce, and operate Cefoperazone Sodium—Tazobactam Sodium for Injection and agreed that the property rights in the drug would be jointly owned by both parties, thereby establishing a relationship of rights and obligations for joint technical development and joint operation. Subsequently, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company and Qili Pharmaceutical Company entered into the "June 8 Agreement" on June 8, 2001, in which they agreed to jointly develop a new drug, Cefoperazone Sodium—Tazobactam Sodium for Injection, in a specification of 1.2g/bottle, and agreed that the property rights in the drug would belong to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, thereby establishing a relationship of rights and obligations for commissioned technical development. After the execution of the above two agreements, Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company entered into the "Transfer Contract" giving rise to this dispute on April 12, 2004, agreeing that Qili Pharmaceutical Company would transfer its product of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection in the specification of 1.125g/bottle to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; the ownership of the product in this specification would belong to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; after Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid the full transfer price, they would exclusively own the product in this specification and be responsible for its production and sale. The content agreed upon by the three parties in the contract indicates that the relationship formed among them was one of rights and obligations for technology transfer. Although the parties to the above three contracts, the drug specifications specified, and the relationships of rights and obligations differed, they were all entered into for the same new drug, namely Cefoperazone Sodium—Tazobactam Sodium for Injection. Although Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were each a party to the "April 26 Agreement" and the "June 8 Agreement," respectively, they were affiliated enterprises. Moreover, in the "June 8 Agreement," Kangli Pharmaceutical Company and Qili Pharmaceutical Company made a new stipulation regarding the ownership of the new drug Cefoperazone Sodium—Tazobactam Sodium for Injection developed by Qili Pharmaceutical Company and limited the validity period of the "April 26 Agreement," to which Kangliyuan Company raised no objection. Thereafter, the stated purpose of signing the "Transfer Contract" by the three parties and their express agreement in that contract to terminate the performance of the "April 26 Agreement" and the "June 8 Agreement" all indicate that the above three contracts were not independent contracts unrelated to each other, and that there was a continuation relationship between the "Transfer Contract" and the "April 26 Agreement" and the "June 8 Agreement." Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's defense that the three contracts were completely independent contracts and that the first two agreements had no relation to this case could not be established, and the court of first instance did not adopt it.

Second, regarding the issue of the subject matter of the transfer under the "Transfer Contract." Qili Pharmaceutical Company defended that its relationship with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company was a transfer of a new drug "product," specifically the transfer of the "product" in the specification of 1.125g/bottle to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and not the transfer of the entire production technology of this new drug to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. The court of first instance held that, according to the agreement of the three parties in the "Transfer Contract," in transferring the product of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection in the specification of 1.125g/bottle to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, Qili Pharmaceutical Company was obligated, in addition to providing Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company with copies of the full set of data for this specification drug, including clinical data, to also cooperate with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in handling the commissioning procedures and to guide Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in continuously producing three batches of qualified products; moreover, after the completion of the transfer, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company would exclusively own the product in this specification and be responsible for its production and sale. The above contract terms indicate that the subject matter of the transfer agreed upon by the three parties was the rights related to the drug technology for Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection in the specification of 1.125g/bottle from Qili Pharmaceutical Company's research and development results. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's defense on this ground could not be established, and the court of first instance did not adopt it.

Third, regarding the validity of Qili Pharmaceutical Company's exercise of the right to terminate the contract. According to Qili Pharmaceutical Company's defense, the main reasons for its exercise of the right to terminate the contract were: First, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company experienced a severe deterioration in their business conditions, lost commercial credibility, and still lacked performance capability within a reasonable period; therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company was entitled to exercise the right of defense for insecurity. Second, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company committed anticipatory breach by failing to perform the payment obligation specified in the "Transfer Contract," thereby preventing Qili Pharmaceutical Company from achieving the purpose of the contract. First, regarding the issue of the right of defense for insecurity raised by Qili Pharmaceutical Company. The so-called right of defense for insecurity means that when the party obligated to perform first has evidence that the party obligated to perform later has experienced a severe deterioration in business conditions, or has transferred property, withdrawn capital, to evade debts, or has lost commercial credibility, or is in any other situation where it has lost or may lose the ability to perform its obligations, the former party may suspend its own performance. In this case, the relationship of rights and obligations between Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company was one of drug technology transfer, i.e., Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were obligated to pay the price to Qili Pharmaceutical Company and entitled to obtain the drug technology, while Qili Pharmaceutical Company was entitled to receive the price and obligated to deliver the drug technology to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. The contract did not stipulate that after the transfer of the agreed drug technology, Qili Pharmaceutical Company would still have the right to participate in the distribution of profits obtained by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company from using the drug technology. Therefore, as the transferor of the drug technology, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's contractual claims were not constrained by the production and sales capabilities of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; as long as Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid the price as agreed, Qili Pharmaceutical Company could realize its expected contractual claims. However, according to the facts found during the trial, the reason Qili Pharmaceutical Company proposed to terminate the contract after obtaining the new drug certificate and drug production approval was not that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had experienced a severe deterioration in financial conditions such that they could not pay the price, jeopardizing Qili Pharmaceutical Company's realization of its contractual claims, but rather that Qili Pharmaceutical Company believed that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had "undergone significant changes, and for a considerable period lacked the basic conditions stipulated by drug administration regulations to accept commissioned processing, making it impossible to perform the original contract." This reason did not meet the statutory conditions for exercising the right of defense for insecurity. Moreover, according to Article 68 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which provides for the right of defense for insecurity, the legal effect of exercising the right of defense for insecurity is that the right holder may suspend the performance of the contract, i.e., the rights and obligations between the parties to the contract are temporarily in a state of suspension, not that the performance of the contract is terminated. Furthermore, although Kangliyuan Company was a shareholder of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, it and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were independent corporate entities. Therefore, even if Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had completely lost the ability to perform the contract due to the revocation of its drug GMP certificate, it should not be concluded that Kangliyuan Company had also lost the ability to perform the contract. Accordingly, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's termination of the contract on the ground of exercising the right of defense for insecurity lacked factual and legal basis. Second, regarding the issue raised by Qili Pharmaceutical Company that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company committed anticipatory breach, thereby preventing Qili Pharmaceutical Company from achieving the purpose of the contract. The so-called anticipatory breach means that before the performance period stipulated in the contract expires, one party clearly indicates, or demonstrates through its conduct, that it will not perform its contractual obligations as agreed. In this case, the three parties clearly stipulated in the "Transfer Contract" the payment of the transfer price, including the initial payment that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company should pay within seven days from the date Qili Pharmaceutical Company obtained the production approval, up to 80% of the price, i.e., RMB 2.4 million. Since the contract provided that Qili Pharmaceutical Company would apply to the national drug regulatory authority for the new drug certificate and production approval, Qili Pharmaceutical Company should have promptly informed Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company after obtaining the new drug certificate and production approval, so that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company could fulfill the payment obligation specified in the contract. However, there was no evidence in this case that Qili Pharmaceutical Company promptly informed Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company after obtaining the new drug certificate and production approval, and that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company refused to pay the price. The evidence submitted by both litigants showed that when Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company learned that Qili Pharmaceutical Company had obtained the new drug certificate and drug production approval, Qili Pharmaceutical Company had already requested termination of the contract on the ground that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company lacked the production capacity for the drug in dispute, leading to a dispute between the parties that culminated in this lawsuit. In fact, regarding the payment of the transfer price by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, in its letter dated August 6, 2007, to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, "Letter on Termination of the 'Transfer Contract' Between the Parties," Qili Pharmaceutical Company requested Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to send representatives to negotiate the refund and contract termination matters; otherwise, it would refund Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company based on the amounts recorded in its financial records. This content indicates that, after the "Transfer Contract" was signed, the three parties had in fact converted the payments made by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company under the "April 26 Agreement" and the "June 8 Agreement" into the transfer price under that contract. Although that amount did not reach the initial payment amount specified in the contract, there was no dispute between the three parties regarding payment before this lawsuit. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's reason for terminating the contract on the ground of anticipatory breach by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company for non-payment could not be established. In summary, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's exercise of the right to terminate the contract did not comply with the law, and the court of first instance did not uphold it.

Fourth, regarding the issue of whether the "Transfer Contract" could continue to be performed. Qili Pharmaceutical Company defended that the "Transfer Contract" could not continue to be performed for two main reasons: First, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were not entitled to produce and sell the drug in dispute; their request that Qili Pharmaceutical Company deliver to them the production and sales rights of this new drug violated prohibitive provisions of the law. Second, Qili Pharmaceutical Company had already produced and sold the new drug on its own and could no longer transfer the new drug to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. Regarding the first reason for non-performance raised by Qili Pharmaceutical Company, the court of first instance held that current national laws or administrative regulations did not impose restrictive provisions on the acceptance of drug technology transfers. Although the reason relied upon by Qili Pharmaceutical Company was Article 80 of the "Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration" promulgated by the State Food and Drug Administration in 2005, which provided that "a pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprise accepting the transfer of new drug technology must hold a 'Drug Manufacturing License' and a certification certificate for 'Good Manufacturing Practices for Pharmaceutical Products'," that administrative regulation had been abolished after the implementation of the newly promulgated "Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration" by the State Food and Drug Administration in 2007, and the newly promulgated administrative regulation did not address this issue. Moreover, even if the relevant administrative regulation had requirements regarding the qualifications of the subject accepting the transfer of new drug technology, according to Article 8 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Technology Contract Dispute Cases," which provides that "where the production of products or provision of services requires approval from relevant authorities or the obtaining of administrative permits by law, but approval or permits have not been obtained, this does not affect the validity of the relevant technology contracts entered into by the parties," it would not affect the contractual rights that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were entitled to enjoy under the contract. As for whether Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had the ability to use the drug technology agreed in the contract after accepting the transfer, and how to use that drug technology, this was subject to supervision by the relevant government functional departments and was unrelated to Qili Pharmaceutical Company. Qili Pharmaceutical Company did not enjoy the right to supervise Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's use of that drug technology either by law or by contract. In fact, Kangliyuan Company, as a drug distribution enterprise, had lawfully obtained drug distribution qualifications before the three parties signed the "Transfer Contract," and those qualifications had not been revoked to date. Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, as a drug manufacturing enterprise, had lawfully obtained drug production qualifications before the three parties signed the "Transfer Contract." During the performance of the contract, although the drug GMP certificates it had obtained were revoked by the Hainan Drug Administration, the "Drug Manufacturing License" it had previously obtained still existed. According to the content of the administrative decision by the Hainan Drug Administration, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company should undergo rectification in accordance with drug GMP standards and, upon completion of the rectification, apply for a review in accordance with legal procedures. It can be seen that Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's original drug production qualifications were not completely lost due to the revocation of its drug GMP certificates by the relevant drug regulatory authority. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's defense on this ground could not be established, and the court of first instance did not adopt it. Regarding Qili Pharmaceutical Company's reliance on Article 46 of the "Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration" newly promulgated by the State Food and Drug Administration in 2007, which provides that "after a new drug application is approved, each variety, including different specifications of the same variety, can only be produced by one entity," as a reason for arguing that since it had already produced and sold the drug on its own after obtaining the new drug certificate and production approval, the contract could no longer be performed, the court of first instance held that the content of the above administrative regulation cited by Qili Pharmaceutical Company was directed at situations where multiple entities jointly develop a new drug. Even if the scope of application of this content was not limited to the aforementioned situation, this content had already existed in the "Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration" promulgated by the State Food and Drug Administration in 2005. Despite the existence of this provision, Qili Pharmaceutical Company still entered into the "Transfer Contract" with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, transferring to them the ownership of the drug in the specification of 1.125g/bottle from its research and development results, and allowing Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to produce and sell the drug in that specification. This was Qili Pharmaceutical Company's disposition of rights related to its own technological achievements. Therefore, in accordance with the principle of good faith stipulated in the General Principles of the Civil Law of China, Qili Pharmaceutical Company should strictly perform its contractual obligations after signing the contract and safeguard the contractual rights that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company were entitled to enjoy under the contract; otherwise, it would constitute a breach of contract. Qili Pharmaceutical Company's defense on this ground lacked legal basis, and the court of first instance did not adopt it.

In summary, the court of first instance held that the "Transfer Contract" entered into by Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company represented the true intent of the three parties, and its contents did not violate any mandatory prohibitions of national laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, it was a valid contract, and all signatory parties should strictly perform their contractual obligations in accordance with the agreement. During the performance of the contract, after Qili Pharmaceutical Company obtained the new drug certificate and drug production approval documents in question, it failed to truthfully inform Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company and instead terminated the contract on the grounds that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company did not have the basic conditions to accept commissioned processing. This conduct constituted a breach of contract, for which Qili Pharmaceutical Company should bear liability for breach according to law. Since Qili Pharmaceutical Company's exercise of the right to terminate the contract did not comply with legal provisions, the "Transfer Contract" entered into by the three parties remained valid, and the three parties should continue to perform their respective contractual obligations as agreed. With respect to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's claim for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cease its breaching conduct, since the "Transfer Contract" provided that after Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid 80% of the transfer price, Qili Pharmaceutical Company undertook not to produce or sell products of the specified specification, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's request for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cease production and sale of products of that specification before paying 80% of the transfer price was inconsistent with the contract. However, after Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid 80% of the transfer price, Qili Pharmaceutical Company should, as agreed, cease production and sale of products of that specification. As for Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's claim for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cease negotiating cooperation or transfer matters with third parties concerning products of that specification, this claim was consistent with the contract, and the court of first instance supported it. With respect to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's claim for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company provide them with a complete set of copies of materials, including clinical data, for Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification: 1.125g/vial), since the contract provided that the above materials were to be delivered after the transfer was completed, and the date of completion of the transfer under the contract was the date on which Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid the full transfer price, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's request for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company deliver the above materials before paying the full transfer price was inconsistent with the contract. However, after Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid the full transfer price, Qili Pharmaceutical Company should perform that contractual obligation as agreed. With respect to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's claim for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company issue relevant documents to facilitate the production and sale by them or their designated enterprise, immediately handle the transfer procedures, return the production right and sales right to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and be responsible for sending personnel to guide Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, or their designated enterprise in continuously producing three batches of conforming products, the court of first instance held that, given that Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had not yet re-obtained the drug GMP certificate and did not yet have the conditions for producing the drugs in question, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's request that Qili Pharmaceutical Company issue relevant documents to them and cooperate in their production contravened the relevant provisions of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and related administrative regulations on the management of drug manufacturing enterprises. As for the issue of production by a drug manufacturing enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, although the three parties did not stipulate in the "Transfer Contract" regarding commissioning a third party for production, since this request by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company complied with Article 13 of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Drug Administration Law), which provides: "With the approval of the drug regulatory department under the State Council or the drug regulatory department of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government authorized by the drug regulatory department under the State Council, a drug manufacturing enterprise may accept commission to manufacture drugs," and it did not increase Qili Pharmaceutical Company's contractual obligations, it was beneficial for the performance of the contract and the maintenance of transactional stability for a drug manufacturing enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company that possessed the conditions for producing the drugs in question to produce the drugs, given that Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had not yet re-obtained the drug GMP certificate and did not yet have the conditions for producing the drugs in question. The court of first instance therefore supported this claim. Accordingly, the court ruled as follows: 1. The "Transfer Contract" entered into by Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall continue to be performed. Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall cease negotiating matters of cooperation or transfer with third parties concerning products of the specifications stipulated in the above contract. After Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company pay 80% of the transfer price, Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall immediately cease production and sale of products of the specifications stipulated in the above contract; after Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company pay the full transfer price, Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall immediately deliver to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company a complete set of copies of the materials stipulated in the above contract. 2. Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall, within the period after the judgment takes legal effect, cooperate with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in handling the procedures for commissioning production, and, after obtaining the approval of the relevant drug regulatory department, transfer the production of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (specification: 1.125g/vial) to a drug manufacturing enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and at the same time send personnel to guide the drug manufacturing enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in continuously producing three batches of conforming products. The products shall be sold by Kangliyuan Company. 3. The other claims of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company are rejected. The court costs of the first instance amounting to RMB 31,800 shall be borne jointly by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company (RMB 9,540) and Qili Pharmaceutical Company (RMB 22,260); the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne jointly by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company.

Qili Pharmaceutical Company, Kangliyuan Company, and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company all appealed against the judgment of the first instance to the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance).

The court of second instance, upon trial, found the following additional facts: During the first instance proceedings, the former Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was approved by the Hainan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce on February 20, 2008, to change its name to Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and its former legal representative, Tang Xudong, was changed to Gao Yuwen. Its former investors were: the Shishang Community Residents' Committee of Jinmao Street, Longhua District, Haikou City, contributing RMB 100,000, representing a 1% share; Hainan Kangdi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., contributing RMB 2,600,000, representing a 26% share; and Kangliyuan Company, contributing RMB 7,300,000, representing a 73% share. After the change, the investors were as follows: the capital contributions and share percentages of the Shishang Community Residents' Committee of Jinmao Street, Longhua District, Haikou City, and Hainan Kangdi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. remained unchanged. Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. transferred shares totaling RMB 5,100,000 (representing a 51% share) out of the RMB 7,300,000 (representing a 73% share) held by Kangliyuan Company to General Technology Group Pharmaceutical Holding Co., Ltd. The registered capital remained RMB 10,000,000. The legal representative of General Technology Group Pharmaceutical Holding Co., Ltd. was also Gao Yuwen. Its investors were General Technology Group Investment Management Co., Ltd., contributing RMB 10,000,000, and China General Technology (Group) Holding Co., Ltd. (a wholly state-owned limited liability company), contributing RMB 190,000,000, with a registered capital of RMB 200,000,000. The court of first instance accordingly changed Haikou Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., i.e., Kangli Pharmaceutical Company as referred to in this case. During the appeal period of this case, the former Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was approved by the Haikou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce on December 30, 2008, to be wholly restructured into Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and published an announcement in "Hainan Daily" on January 5, 2009. The company's promoters were four enterprises — Haikou Dongkong Industrial Co., Ltd., Guangdong Provincial Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Guangdong Guangrun Investment Co., Ltd., Haikou Free Trade Zone Development and Construction Corporation — and ten natural-person shareholders. The total subscribed shares were 97,000,000. Among them, Guangdong Provincial Venture Capital Co., Ltd. and Haikou Free Trade Zone Development and Construction Corporation were state-owned companies, holding a combined total of 14,530,000 shares, accounting for 15% of the total shares. The court of second instance accordingly changed Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., i.e., Qili Pharmaceutical Company as referred to in this case. After the judgment of first instance was served, Kangliyuan Company, on November 25 and December 8, 2008, obtained notarial certificates (2008) Qiongya Zheng No. 11554 and No. 12027 from the Qiongya Notary Public Office in Haikou City, Hainan Province, notarizing the deposit of RMB 200,000 and RMB 600,000, and the notary office issued a notice of collection to Qili Pharmaceutical Company. During the second instance proceedings, on February 21, 2009, the Hainan Provincial Drug Administration (Hainan PDA) replied to Qili Pharmaceutical Company by letter (Qiong Shi Yao Jian Zhu Han [2009] No. 9), stating: An application for new drug technology transfer shall be filed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Drug Registration Administration Measures" (Order No. 28 of the State Drug Administration). Whether approval can be granted is decided by the State Drug Administration. On March 11, 2009, the Hainan PDA issued a change to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's drug manufacturing license, adding the following production scope: freeze-dried powder injections and powder injections (both cephalosporins). During the second instance proceedings, the court of second instance consulted the Hainan PDA, which replied on March 13, 2009, by letter (Qiong Shi Yao Jian Zhu Han [2009] No. 13), stating: 1. According to the drug registration approvals (Nos. 2007S00839 and 2007S00840) issued by the State Drug Administration (see Appendix 1), Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (8:1) produced by Qili Pharmaceutical Company is a Category 1.5 new chemical drug (new drug certificate number: National Drug Certificate H20070099), being a new compound preparation not yet marketed domestically or internationally. A search of the State Drug Administration website's basic drug database query system shows that Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (8:1) is exclusively owned by Qili Pharmaceutical Company (see Appendix 2). 2. Regarding the new drug technology transfer of Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (8:1), our bureau may apply Article 10(2) of the "Notice on Issuing Supplementary Provisions on Drug Registration Administration" (Guo Shi Yao Jian Zhu [2002] No. 367) of the State Drug Administration, which provides: "Where during the monitoring period only one enterprise has obtained production registration, a new drug technology transfer may be carried out," as well as relevant state provisions and conditions to accept the application for new drug technology transfer and report it to the State Drug Administration for approval. 3. Kangli Pharmaceutical Company meets the conditions for adding the production scope of "cephalosporin powder injections" and on March 11, 2009, obtained from our bureau a license for the newly added production scope of powder injections and freeze-dried powder injections (both cephalosporin powder injections) (see Appendix 3). Upon obtaining the drug approval number for this dosage form, it may apply for the "Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products" certification for the new dosage form in accordance with Article 6 of the Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law. 4. Drug manufacturing enterprises with a corresponding production scope in the "Drug Manufacturing License" and a GMP certificate, as well as newly established enterprises or new workshops with a corresponding production scope in the "Drug Manufacturing License", may serve as transferees for new drug technology transfers. Other facts found by the court of second instance were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the issues in dispute in this case were: (1) the validity of the "Transfer Contract" and whether it should continue to be performed, etc.; (2) the relationship among the "April 26 Agreement," the "June 8 Agreement," and the "Transfer Contract," the actual amount of payment, and whether repayment was required, etc.; (3) the breaching conduct of both parties during the performance of the contract and the allocation of liability, etc.

1. Regarding the validity of the "Transfer Contract" and whether it should continue to be performed, etc. Article 34 of the Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law) provides: "The drug regulatory department under the State Council may, based on the need to protect public health, establish a monitoring period of no more than five years for new drugs produced by drug manufacturing enterprises; during the monitoring period, other enterprises shall not be approved to produce or import the drug." In this case, the new drug certificate (No. H20070099) and drug registration approval (No. 2007S00839) for Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (1.125g/vial) developed by Qili Pharmaceutical Company were issued by the State Drug Administration on May 21, 2007, indicating that the manufacturing enterprise was Qili Pharmaceutical Company, with a monitoring period of 4 years until May 20, 2011. Regarding technology transfer and commissioned production of new drugs, Article 66 of the "Drug Registration Administration Measures" (implemented in October 2007) of the State Drug Administration provides: "The State Drug Administration may, based on the need to protect public health, establish a monitoring period for new drug varieties approved for production. The monitoring period shall commence from the date of approval of new drug production, with a maximum of five years. During the monitoring period for a new drug, the State Drug Administration shall not approve other enterprises to produce, change dosage forms, or import the drug." Commissioned production means that an enterprise that has obtained a drug approval number, after undergoing approval according to law, entrusts the production of the drug to an enterprise that has the statutory production conditions and qualifications, but the commissioning enterprise is responsible for the quality and sale of the commissioned drug. Article 10 of the Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law provides: "In accordance with Article 13 of the Drug Administration Law, where a drug manufacturing enterprise accepts commission to manufacture drugs, the commission-receiving party must be a drug manufacturing enterprise holding a certificate of compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products for the drug it is commissioned to manufacture." Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "The 'mandatory provisions' referred to in Article 52(5) of the Contract Law mean mandatory provisions regarding validity." According to the above provisions, although the "Transfer Contract" signed by the parties violated the provisions of the Implementing Regulations of the Drug Administration Law, the above regulations are not mandatory provisions regarding validity. The "Drug Registration Administration Measures" (implemented in 2007) is a departmental regulation of the State Drug Administration, and failure to comply with it does not affect the validity of the contract. Therefore, the "Transfer Contract" entered into by Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company should be a valid contract. Qili Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that the contract was invalid had no factual or legal basis. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that the contract was valid had a factual and legal basis and should be adopted. At the time of signing, Kangliyuan Company, as a drug distribution unit, held a "Drug Distribution License" and a "Certificate of Compliance with Good Distribution Practice for Pharmaceutical Products"; Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, as a drug manufacturing unit, also held a "Drug Manufacturing License" and a drug GMP certificate. However, during the performance of the contract, an inspection team composed of the State Drug Administration and the Hainan PDA conducted an on-site inspection on December 31, 2006, and found that Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's drug production did not meet the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice. Authorized by the State Drug Administration, the Hainan PDA revoked the company's six drug GMP certificates and required it to rectify in accordance with GMP standards and apply for re-inspection through legal procedures after completion of rectification. During the second instance proceedings, the Hainan PDA issued to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company a license for the production scope corresponding to the drugs in question. However, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had not yet obtained a drug GMP certificate corresponding to the drugs in question. Drugs are different from ordinary goods and commodities; they directly concern the life, health, and safety of the general public. Therefore, all aspects of drug research and development, approval, production, including commissioned production, transfer, transportation, storage, sale, and use, must be strictly carried out in accordance with laws, regulations, rules, and operating procedures. Pursuant to Article 94 of the Contract Law: "A contract may be terminated under any of the following circumstances: (1) the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved due to force majeure; ..." Article 117(2) provides: "Force majeure as used in this Law means objective circumstances that cannot be foreseen, cannot be avoided, and cannot be overcome." Because the State Drug Administration revoked Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's drug GMP certificate, and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to date has not obtained from the State Drug Administration a drug GMP certificate corresponding to the cephalosporin freeze-dried powder injections and powder injections for producing the drugs in question, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company no longer possesses the statutory qualification conditions to produce the drugs in question. Therefore, due to the change in the above objective circumstances, the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved. The "Transfer Contract" entered into by Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall be terminated according to law. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that the contract could not be performed and should be terminated had a factual and legal basis and should be supported. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that the contract should continue to be performed and that Qili Pharmaceutical Company should be ordered to cease production and sale and immediately handle the transfer procedures had no factual or legal basis.

2. Regarding the relationship among the three contracts and the actual amount of payment and whether repayment was required, etc. The "April 26 Agreement" entered into by Kangliyuan Company and Qili Pharmaceutical Company was, in nature, a technology cooperation development and cooperation operation agreement. The first instance found that Kangliyuan Company paid RMB 100,000 to Qili Pharmaceutical Company on April 28, 2000; RMB 100,000 on June 8, 2000; RMB 200,000 on August 31, 2000; and RMB 100,000 on November 27, 2000. On June 8, 2001, Qili Pharmaceutical Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company entered into the "June 8 Agreement," which was, in nature, a technology commission development agreement. The first instance found that Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid RMB 250,000 to Qili Pharmaceutical Company on July 18, 2001; RMB 250,000 on September 21, 2001; and RMB 100,000 on October 15, 2002. After the three parties signed the "Transfer Contract" on June 12, 2004, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company did not make any further payments to Qili Pharmaceutical Company. The "Transfer Contract" explicitly stipulated that upon its entry into force, the contracts signed on April 26, 2000, and June 8, 2001, would automatically lapse. Therefore, the first two contracts were no longer binding on the three parties. However, the subject matter of all three contracts pertained to the research and development of the new drug Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium; the first contract specified a specification of 1g/vial, the second contract specified a specification of 1.2g/vial, and the third contract specified a specification of 1.125g/vial. Thus, the research and development of the subject matter was continuous. In the proceedings, Qili Pharmaceutical Company also stated that it had spent seven years on research and development before obtaining the new drug certificate and production approval. The evidence in this case showed that in the early stage of the research and development, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company made a total payment of RMB 1,100,000 under the two contracts. When the two contracts were terminated, no provision was made regarding the funds. However, in the letter sent by Qili Pharmaceutical Company on August 6, 2007, to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company terminating the contract, it stated that if no one came to negotiate by August 20, it would be deemed as termination of the contract and a refund would be made based on the amount recorded in the financial records. Since the court of second instance had terminated the new drug "Transfer Contract" signed on June 12, 2004, according to law, pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law, after a contract is terminated, for performance that has already been rendered, restitution may be made depending on the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company should refund RMB 500,000 to Kangliyuan Company and RMB 600,000 to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, totaling RMB 1,100,000, plus interest accrued during the period of its possession. Accordingly, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that it had not received payments from Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had no factual or legal basis. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's assertion on appeal that they had paid the full RMB 3,000,000 in research and development expenses was accepted by the court of second instance to the extent of RMB 1,100,000 paid; the remaining portion had no factual or legal basis and was not supported.

3. Regarding the issues of breach of contract by both parties during performance and how liability should be allocated. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company entered into the New Drug Transfer Contract on June 12, 2004. Both parties were obligated to fully perform their respective duties in accordance with the contract. However, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company failed to maintain the statutory qualifications required to receive the production of the contracted drugs as agreed. Because its drug production did not comply with the national requirements for drug production quality management, the National Medical Products Administration authorized the Hainan Medical Products Administration to revoke its drug GMP certificate, rendering it to this day without the statutory qualifications to produce the drugs involved in the case. Both Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company failed to pay, in accordance with the contract, 80% of the 3 million yuan transfer payment as agreed, i.e., 2.4 million yuan, and the remaining 600,000 yuan on time. These acts all violated the contract. After Qili Pharmaceutical Company obtained the new drug certificate and drug registration approval on May 21, 2007, it failed to perform the transfer and handle the entrustment processing procedures as stipulated in the contract, which also constituted a breach of contract. Therefore, during the performance of the New Drug Transfer Contract, both parties had acts of breach, causing the purpose of the contract to be unattainable. Consequently, the court of second instance lawfully dissolved the New Drug Transfer Contract. During the trial, the court of second instance repeatedly presided over mediation between Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company. During mediation, Qili Pharmaceutical Company indicated that the production and sale of the drugs involved in the case would be entirely enjoyed by Qili Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company undertook to compensate Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company 18 million yuan, to be paid in full within three years. The court of second instance held that Qili Pharmaceutical Company's request to settle by compensating Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company 18 million yuan represented Qili Pharmaceutical Company's true intention, did not violate legal provisions, and was lawfully approved. This compensation amount was sufficient to cover all losses of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company after the lawful dissolution of the contract. The court of second instance determined that the compensation payment must be made within three months. Because both parties had acts of breach during performance and were subjectively at fault, each should bear corresponding liability. Therefore, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company should bear the legal consequences of the contract being lawfully dissolved, i.e., the Transfer Contract between the parties ceased performance, and Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company lawfully did not enjoy or assume rights and obligations under the contract. Qili Pharmaceutical Company should bear the legal consequences of compensating Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company 18 million yuan, i.e., ownership of the involved new drug cefoperazone sodium and tazobactam sodium (specification 1.125g/bottle) belonged to Qili Pharmaceutical Company. Accordingly, the appellate claims of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company that they had no breach and that it was Qili Pharmaceutical Company's unilateral breach, as well as Qili Pharmaceutical Company's appellate claim that it had no breach and that it was Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's unilateral breach, all lacked factual and legal basis and were not supported by the court of second instance.

In summary, the first instance judgment found the facts clearly, but applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected. The court of second instance ruled: 1. Set aside the first instance judgment; 2. Dissolve the Transfer Contract entered into by Kangliyuan Company, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company on June 12, 2004; 3. Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of the judgment, return 500,000 yuan and interest to Kangliyuan Company (calculated from April 29, 2000, on 100,000 yuan; from June 9, 2000, on 200,000 yuan; from August 31, 2000, on 400,000 yuan; from November 28, 2000, on 500,000 yuan, using the People's Bank of China's one-year floating loan interest rate for working capital until the date of full payment); 4. Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of the judgment, return 600,000 yuan and interest to Kangli Pharmaceutical Company (calculated from July 19, 2001, on 250,000 yuan; from September 22, 2001, on 500,000 yuan; from October 16, 2002, on 600,000 yuan, using the People's Bank of China's one-year floating loan interest rate for working capital until the date of full payment); 5. Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall, within three months from the effective date of the judgment, pay 18 million yuan in compensation to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; 6. Dismiss the other appellate claims of Qili Pharmaceutical Company; 7. Dismiss the other appellate claims of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. The first instance case acceptance fee of 31,800 yuan, the second instance case acceptance fee of 31,800 yuan, and the preservation fee of 5,000 yuan, totaling 68,600 yuan, shall be borne by Qili Pharmaceutical Company in the amount of 34,300 yuan, and jointly borne by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in the amount of 34,300 yuan.

Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, alleging: (1) Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had already paid 3 million yuan to Qili Pharmaceutical Company, fulfilling and exceeding the payment obligation ahead of schedule. 1. The 1.1 million yuan paid by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company during the performance of the April 26 Agreement and the June 8 Agreement had been transferred into the research and development of the disputed drug; 2. The 250,000 yuan in research and development fees paid by Kangliyuan Company for the development of cefoperazone sodium-sulbactam sodium drug had been converted into the transfer payment for the disputed new drug; 3.
