On July 29, 2006, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, at the request of Qili Pharmaceutical Company, remitted 850,000 yuan to Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Research Institute Co., Ltd. for the research and development of the disputed new drug; 4. Kangliyuan Company deposited 800,000 yuan with the Hainan Province Haikou Qiongya Notary Public Office, thereby fulfilling the obligation to pay the remaining balance of the contract; 5. In the letter dated August 6, 2007, from Qili Pharmaceutical Company to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, titled "Regarding the Termination of the Transfer Contract Between the Parties," the statement that "Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company should send personnel to negotiate refund and contract termination matters, otherwise it will refund according to the financial records amount" indicated that Qili Pharmaceutical Company had admitted to receiving 2.2 million yuan in transfer payment for the disputed new drug from Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company.

(2) The court of second instance's decision to dissolve the Transfer Contract based on Article 94, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law was an erroneous application of law. 1. The performance of the Transfer Contract faced no factual or legal obstacles. The revocation of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's drug GMP certificate by the National Medical Products Administration was a situation that could be overcome. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had the ability to continue performing the Transfer Contract. The court of second instance's dissolution of the contract on the grounds that "force majeure made the contract purpose unattainable" was erroneous. (1) Kangliyuan Company had always held a Drug Business License and Drug Business Quality Management Practice Certification, fully possessing sales capacity and the ability to continue performing the Transfer Contract; (2) Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's original drug production qualification had not been completely lost due to the temporary revocation of the drug GMP certificate; (3) According to Article 79 of the Contract Law and Article 21 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Technology Contract Dispute Cases, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had the right to request Qili Pharmaceutical Company to assign the production right of the disputed new drug to Hainan Xin Zhong Zheng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., which had production capacity and was designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company; (4) According to relevant laws, regulations, and rules of China, new drugs within the monitoring period could be transferred lawfully. 2. Continued performance of the Transfer Contract could fully achieve the purpose of the contract as originally intended by both parties. As long as Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid the price as agreed, Qili Pharmaceutical Company could achieve its expected contract purpose. As for whether Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had the ability to use and how to use the drug technology after receiving it, that was subject to supervision by relevant government functional departments and had nothing to do with Qili Pharmaceutical Company. 3. During the first instance trial, Qili Pharmaceutical Company expressed an intention to continue performing the contract. Under circumstances where both parties agreed to perform, the court of second instance's interference with "private rights of contract" by public power was a serious error.

(3) The court of second instance's order that "Qili Pharmaceutical Company shall pay 18 million yuan in compensation to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company within three months from the effective date of this judgment" exceeded the claims of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, violating the basic principle of "no trial without complaint." Qili Pharmaceutical Company, by using the technology and products involved, earned at least 80 million yuan annually, totaling approximately 240 million yuan in illegal profits to date. According to the principle of equality of rights and obligations, if the judgment were to be changed, it should order Qili Pharmaceutical Company to pay 240 million yuan in compensation. Moreover, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had made substantial investments to perform the Transfer Contract, and Qili Pharmaceutical Company's breach had caused losses of nearly 200 million yuan to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company.

In summary, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2), (6), and (12) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting this Court to set aside the second instance judgment and uphold their claims.

Qili Pharmaceutical Company submitted its opinion, stating: (1) Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had not paid any amount under the Transfer Contract and had already breached the contract in advance, thus not entitled to request continued performance. 1. The 1.1 million yuan paid by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company before June 12, 2004, was not payment under the Transfer Contract and was unrelated to this case. 2. The 850,000 yuan paid by Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Research Institute Co., Ltd. on July 24, 2006, was unrelated to this case. 3. Kangliyuan Company's claim that it had deposited 800,000 yuan did not prove it had not breached in advance. 4. The 250,000 yuan in research and development fees for cefoperazone sodium-sulbactam sodium paid by Kangliyuan Company to Qili Pharmaceutical Company was unrelated to this case. 5. Qili Pharmaceutical Company had no obligation to remind Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to pay the transfer price. (2) The Transfer Contract, being in violation of mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations and harming public interest, was lawfully invalid. 1. The Transfer Contract violated the provisions that new drug technology within the monitoring period could not be transferred, and that other enterprises could not be approved for production and import. 2. The transferee under the Transfer Contract did not meet the statutory conditions for receiving the new drug technology involved and lacked the qualification as a lawful subject. 3. The provisions in the Transfer Contract regarding the handover of technical materials and Qili Pharmaceutical Company's retention of the production approval violated the provisions of the Drug Registration Regulation (Trial). 4. The Transfer Contract violated the provision that all specifications of a new drug technology must be transferred to one drug production enterprise at one time. 5. The Transfer Contract violated the provisions of the Drug Production Supervision and Administration Regulation concerning that the entrusting party must sign an entrustment production contract with the entrusted party, and regulations on "quality and sales" of entrusted production drugs. 6. The Transfer Contract harmed social public interest and should be invalid. (3) Even if the Transfer Contract were valid, it should be dissolved due to "factual and legal impossibility of performance" and "the subject matter of the contract not being suitable for compulsory performance." Qili Pharmaceutical Company's unilateral dissolution of the contract on August 6, 2007, was lawful and effective and should be upheld. 1. The provisions of the Transfer Contract regarding new drug transfer (or entrusted production) conflicted with national laws and regulations, making the contract legally unperformable. 2. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company did not possess the statutory "Injectable Powder Cephalosporin Category" Drug Production License and drug GMP certificate required to produce the new drug involved, so the Transfer Contract was factually unperformable. 3. The subject matter of the contract was not suitable for compulsory enforcement. If the judgment ordered Qili Pharmaceutical Company to continue performing, the judgment would be not only factually and legally unperformable but also unenforceable. (4) Even if the Transfer Contract were lawful and valid, since Kangli Pharmaceutical Company subsequently lost the "Injectable Powder Cephalosporin Category" Drug Production License and drug GMP certificate, violating the mandatory provisions of the state on franchising of drug production, rendering the contract legally unperformable, it should be dissolved. Therefore, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's dissolution of the contract was proper. (5) Even if the Transfer Contract were lawful and valid, since Qili Pharmaceutical Company had notified Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company of the dissolution of the contract on August 6, 2007, but Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company did not file a lawsuit with the People's Court to raise objections until January 1, 2008, i.e., three months after receiving the dissolution notice, the People's Court should dismiss it according to law. (6) Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had no right and never requested to transfer their rights under the New Drug Transfer Contract to a third party. Their request in the retrial application that they had the right to require Qili Pharmaceutical Company to transfer the disputed new drug technology to their designated unit was not legally sustainable. (7) The reason the Transfer Contract was not performed was entirely due to the fault of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company. Qili Pharmaceutical Company should not bear liability for breach or compensation. In summary, the retrial application of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

Upon retrial, this Court finds that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance are generally true.

This Court holds that the disputed issues in this case are: (1) the validity of the Transfer Contract; (2) the performance and breach of the Transfer Contract; (3) whether the Transfer Contract should continue to be performed; and (4) the assumption of liability for breach.

(1) Regarding the validity of the Transfer Contract.

The Transfer Contract stipulated that Qili Pharmaceutical Company (Party A) would, after obtaining approval for the new drug involved, transfer the product in the specification of 1.125g/bottle to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company (Party B), but the production unit indicated on the product's production approval would remain Party A, with Party A entrusting Party B to produce; the date when Party B paid the full transfer price would be the date of completion of the transfer, after which ownership of the product in that specification would belong to Party B; the transfer price was 3 million yuan, with Party B paying 2.4 million yuan within 7 days from obtaining the production approval, and 600,000 yuan within 7 days from completing the entrustment processing procedures. Therefore, the Transfer Contract involved both the transfer of new drug technology and the entrustment of new drug production.

Regarding the transfer of new drug technology, the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Drug Administration Law") and its implementing regulations do not contain specific provisions. This issue has always been regulated by the National Medical Products Administration through administrative regulations and normative documents. Considering the drug management regulations in effect at the time the parties entered into the Transfer Contract, there were no mandatory provisions in laws or administrative regulations concerning the transfer of new drug technology. Although administrative regulations had specific provisions on the transfer of new drug technology, according to Article 52, item (5) of the Contract Law, the parties' agreement on the transfer of new drug technology in the Transfer Contract, even if it violated administrative regulations, did not fall within the circumstances where the contract is invalid for violating mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, the parties' agreement on the transfer of new drug technology in this case is valid, and both parties should perform accordingly.

Regarding the entrustment of drug production, Article 13 of the Drug Administration Law provides that a drug production enterprise, subject to approval by the relevant drug regulatory authority, may accept entrustment to produce drugs. Article 10 of the Implementing Regulation of the Drug Administration Law provides that the entrusted party must hold a drug GMP certificate appropriate for the drugs it is entrusted to produce. At the time the parties entered into the Transfer Contract, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company held a Drug Production License and a drug GMP certificate appropriate for the new drug involved. Therefore, the parties' agreement to entrust Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to produce the new drug involved did not violate the provisions of laws and administrative regulations. Kangliyuan Company was not a drug production enterprise and could not accept entrustment to produce drugs. Although the Transfer Contract did not distinguish the specific rights and obligations of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company as Party B in the contract, based on Kangliyuan Company's qualifications as a drug business enterprise, its role in the contract should be to sell the new drug involved, not to produce it. Therefore, the parties' agreement on the entrustment of drug production in this case did not violate the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and is valid. Both parties should also perform accordingly.

Article 8, paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Technology Contract Dispute Cases provides that if the production of a product or the provision of a service is subject to approval or an administrative license from a relevant department, and such approval or license has not been obtained, this does not affect the validity of the relevant technology contract entered into by the parties. Therefore, whether Kangli Pharmaceutical Company could obtain a Drug Production License and a drug GMP certificate for the production of the new drug involved does not affect the validity of the Transfer Contract. In conclusion, the Transfer Contract should be determined to be a valid contract. The courts of first and second instance correctly determined that the Transfer Contract was valid, and this determination should be upheld.

(2) Regarding the performance and breach of the Transfer Contract.

From the established facts, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company paid a total of 1.1 million yuan in research and development fees to Qili Pharmaceutical Company in performing the April 26 Agreement and the June 8 Agreement. Since the April 26 Agreement and the June 8 Agreement, along with the Transfer Contract, were all contracts entered into for the same new drug, cefoperazone sodium tazobactam sodium, and were continuous in nature, and since Qili Pharmaceutical Company, in its August 6, 2007 letter on termination of the Transfer Contract, requested Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to send personnel to negotiate refund and contract termination, otherwise it would refund according to the financial records, Qili Pharmaceutical Company's contention that Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had not paid any amount under the Transfer Contract lacks factual and legal basis. This Court upholds Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's assertion that the 1.1 million yuan in research and development fees paid under the April 26 Agreement and the June 8 Agreement had been converted into the Transfer Contract price.

Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company also argued: (1) The research and development expenses of RMB 250,000 paid by Kangliyuan Company for the development of Cefoperazone Sodium – Sulbactam Sodium had been converted into the transfer price for the new drug in dispute, but such amount was not used for the research and development of the new drug under the "Transfer Contract"; (2) On July 29, 2006, Kangli Pharmaceutical Company remitted RMB 850,000 to Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Research Institute Co., Ltd. as the already paid transfer price, but such amount was not paid to Qili Pharmaceutical Company, and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company also failed to provide evidence to prove that such amount had actually been transferred to Qili Pharmaceutical Company; (3) After the service of the judgment of first instance, Kangliyuan Company deposited RMB 800,000 as the already paid transfer price with Qiongya Notary Public Office, Haikou City, Hainan Province on November 25, 2008, but such deposit did not meet the conditions for deposit prescribed in Article 101, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law. Therefore, this Court does not support the claims of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company that the above three sums totaling RMB 1.9 million constituted the transfer price paid for the performance of the "Transfer Contract."

According to the terms of the "Transfer Contract," the transfer price was RMB 3 million. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company should pay 80%, i.e., RMB 2.4 million, within seven days from the date of obtaining the production approval document for the new drug in dispute, and pay the remaining 20% balance of RMB 600,000 within seven days from the date of completing the entrusted processing procedures. Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company had paid RMB 1.1 million before the date of obtaining the production approval document for the new drug in dispute. After obtaining the production approval document for the new drug in dispute, Qili Pharmaceutical Company did not timely notify Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to pay the remaining price, but instead organized its own production and sales. Qili Pharmaceutical Company's conduct violated the terms of the "Transfer Contract" and constituted a breach of contract.

(3) Whether the "Transfer Contract" should continue to be performed

From the specific content of the "Transfer Contract," after Qili Pharmaceutical Company obtained the new drug certificate and production approval document, it delivered to Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company the complete set of documents of the product (specification: 1.125g/vial) covered by the new drug certificate and production approval document, and cooperated with Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in handling the entrusted processing procedures, thereby fulfilling its obligation of new drug technology transfer under the contract. At the same time, it could notify Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to pay the contract price and realize its contractual claim. Of course, according to the contract terms, 20% of the transfer price, i.e., RMB 600,000, was subject to the condition of completing the entrusted processing procedures. If the payment condition could not be met because Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company lacked the qualifications for entrusted production, Qili Pharmaceutical Company could claim such amount through negotiation or other means, thereby realizing its contractual claim. As to whether the new drug assigned under the "Transfer Contract" could obtain administrative approval and whether Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company could produce it after the assignment, such matters should be supervised by the relevant government functional departments, and the consequences should naturally be borne by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company, which were unrelated to Qili Pharmaceutical Company's realization of its contractual claim. Therefore, the claim of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company for continued performance of the contract is established. The defense of Qili Pharmaceutical Company that the content of the "Transfer Contract" could not be performed because it violated the administrative approval regulations for drugs and thus required rescission of the contract is untenable. The judgment of first instance, which ordered Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to continue to perform their respective contractual obligations in accordance with the "Transfer Contract," correctly applied the law and should be upheld. The judgment of second instance, which rescinded the contract on the ground that the revocation of Kangli Pharmaceutical Company's drug GMP certificate constituted a force majeure event, erroneously applied the law and should be corrected.

The request of Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company for continued performance of the contract should be supported. However, their request for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cease production and sale of the drug in dispute is inconsistent with the terms of the "Transfer Contract" because they have not yet paid 80% of the transfer price. The court of first instance was not improper in denying such request. As to their request for an order that Qili Pharmaceutical Company cooperate with the enterprise designated by them in producing and selling the new drug product in dispute, since such request was not provided for in the "Transfer Contract," the court of first instance's support for such request violated the principle of party autonomy and was clearly improper and should be corrected.

(4) Regarding the assumption of liability for breach of contract

As discussed above, after obtaining the new drug certificate and drug production approval document for the drug in dispute, Qili Pharmaceutical Company did not timely notify Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company to make payment, but instead produced and sold the drug in dispute on its own, failing to perform the obligation of transferring the technology for the drug in dispute. Such conduct constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach. However, Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company only requested continued performance of the contract and did not seek other compensation or damages. Therefore, the judgment of second instance, which ordered Qili Pharmaceutical Company to compensate Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company RMB 18 million, exceeded the litigants' claims and should be corrected.

In summary, the judgment of second instance erroneously applied the law and should be corrected. The judgment of first instance, which ordered Qili Pharmaceutical Company to cooperate with the enterprise designated by Kangliyuan Company and Kangli Pharmaceutical Company in producing and selling the new drug product in dispute, was clearly improper. However, the first instance judgment correctly found the other facts and correctly applied the law. Pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 8 and 60 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2009) Qiong Min Er Zhong Zi No. 16 of the Hainan High People's Court is hereby vacated;

2. Items 1 and 3 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2008) Hai Zhong Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 19 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, Hainan Province are affirmed;

3. Item 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2008) Hai Zhong Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 19 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, Hainan Province is amended as follows: After this judgment takes legal effect, Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. shall cooperate with Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in handling the entrusted production procedures. Upon approval by the relevant drug regulatory authority, Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. shall deliver the injectable Cefoperazone Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium (specification: 1.125 g/vial) to Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. for production and sale, and simultaneously dispatch personnel to guide Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the continuous production of three batches of qualified products.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 31,800. This shall be borne jointly by Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 9,540, and by Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 22,260. Property preservation fee: RMB 5,000, jointly borne by Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 31,800. This shall be borne by Haikou Qili Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 15,900, and jointly by Hainan Kangliyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Hainan General Kangli Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 15,900.

This judgment is final.
